newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Tel jumps on renewed stake sale talk.
newsitem.headline: HK Tel jumps on renewed stake sale talk.

text.p: Shares in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd bucked a generally weak tone in the Hong Kong stock market on Wednesday, moving higher on renewed expectations that a Chinese partner would buy a stake in the company, brokers said.
The stock was up HK$0.30, or 2.18 percent, at HK$14.05 in mid-morning trade on volume of 18.88 million shares.
"The shares have underperformed for quite a while and many have taken the expectations as an excuse to switch into the utility stock," said a sales manager at a regional brokerage.
A spokesman at Hong Kong Telecommunications declined to comment on a possible new shareholder for the company.

Brokers said the market expected Hongkong Telecom parent Cable and Wireless Plc to sell part of its stake in the company to a Chinese entity which would improve Hongkong Telecom's prospects for doing business in the mainland.

"We expect the stock to trade in a range of HK$13 to HK$17 in near run. The top of the range represents a reasonable P/E (price/earnings) level of about 18 times," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
The stock is currently trading at about 16 times earnings, he said.
